To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Models trained with different training methodology exhibit increasingly uncorrelated generalization behavior, and (2) Models trained with divergent methodology capture overlapping feature sets, and when combined lead to increased ensemble performance.

(1) models trained with different methods specialize in different subdomains of the input data, leading to uncorrelated errors, (2) ensembling these models leads to improved generalization performance, and (3) representations learned by these models overlap but do not necessarily capture all of the features of the input data.
\textit{Overlapping features of training methods lead to complementary representations that can improve downstream performance and ensemble accuracy, even when the models have low accuracy.}

the following questions: (1) What is the relationship between training methods and model behavior, (2) Can we use this insight to improve model ensembles, and (3) How do representations trained with different methods relate to each other?
